GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
DEPARTMENT OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
 
RAJYA  SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 913 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 09.02.2022 
 
 
SCOPE AND POTENTIAL OF WORKS UNDER MGNREGS 
 
913  SHRI K.R.N. RAJESHKUMAR: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether there is a lot of scope and potential for taking up works under Mahatma 
Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS) which would not 
only 
benefit farmers but also help in creation of assets; 
(b)  if so, whether Government has identified such works to be done under MGNREGS; 
(c)  if so, the details thereof; and 
(d)  whether Government has reviewed the implementation of MGNREGS, drinking water 
schemes and other works recently and if so, the outcome thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRI FAGGAN SINGH KULASTE) 
 
(a) to (c):    Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (Mahatma Gandhi 
NREGS) is a demand driven wage employment programme. The core objective of the scheme is 
to provide not less than one hundred days of unskilled manual work as a guaranteed employment 
in a financial year to every household in rural areas as per demand, resulting in creation of 
productive assets of prescribed quality and durability and to strengthen the livelihood resource 
base of the poor. 
  
As per para 4(2) of Schedule 1 of Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act 
(Mahatma Gandhi NREGA), the District Programme Coordinator (DPC) shall ensure that 
at least 
60% of the works to be taken up in a district in terms of cost shall be for creation of productive 
assets directly linked to agriculture and allied activities through development of land, water and 
trees. 
  
The Ministry also focus on individual beneficiaries works by improving productivity of lands of 
households specified in paragraph 5 through land development, by providing suitable 
infrastructure for irrigation, by improving livelihoods through horticulture, sericulture, plantation 
and farm forestry and by creating infrastructure for promotion of livestock and fisheries. 
 
 
There are 262 types of permissible works out of which 182 works are related to Natural Resource 
Management (NRM) and 164 works are related to agriculture and allied activities. The list of 164 
permissible works related to agriculture and allied activities is given at Annexure. 
340

(d):    The review of implementation of Mahatma Gandhi NREGS is done on regular basis and 
necessary improvements are made accordingly. The system of geo-tagging of assets, National 
Electronic Fund Management System (NeFMS)  for direct wage payment into the account of 
beneficiaries, the functioning of social audit units, GIS based planning by Gram Panchayats are 
the subjects/outcomes of the regular review of the scheme.  
  
As per information shared by Ministry of Jal Shakti, the Ministry in partnership with States is 
implementing Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) – Har Ghar Jal, which aims at providing potable water in 
adequate quantity of prescribed quality on regular and long-term basis to every rural household, 
through tap water connection. 
 
 
As water is a State subject, it is the States who plan, design, implement, operate and maintain the 
water supply schemes. Central Government only supplements the efforts of State Governments 
by providing technical and financial assistance for successful implementation of drinking water 
projects in rural areas. 
 
 
Under JJM, provision has been made that Village Action Plan (VAPs) is to be prepared. All 
States have been advised that while preparing Village Action Plan, dovetailing of resources 
available at village level under various programmes like 15 th Finance Commission tied grant for 
water & sanitation, JJM, Swachh Bharat Mission-Gramin, Mahatma Gandhi NREGS, District 
Mineral Development Fund, CSR fund, community contributions, etc. are to 
 be taken up for 
long-term water security of the village;”

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
 
RAJYA SABHA 
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 914 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 09.02.2022 
  
TECHNOLOGICAL TRAINING CENTRES 
 
914. LT.GEN. (DR.) D. P. VATS (RETD.): 
  
Will the Minister of SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP be pleased 
to state: 
  
(a) the details of technological training centres in the country to meet the technological 
changes upgradation to compete with the foreign manufacturers, State-wise and sector-wise; 
 
(
b)  whether Government has taken a decision to establish a technological training 
centre/industrial hub in the country to enhance the skill of employees; and 
 
(
c) if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
  
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE 
MINISTRY OF SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
(SHRI RAJEEV CHANDRASEKHAR) 
 
(a) Under Skill India Mission, Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) 
through its various schemes such as Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) and 
Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS) is delivering training to meet technological changes to 
compete with foreign manufacturers. However, there are no centres by the name of 
Technological Training Centre under any scheme of the Ministry. 
 
Under PMKVY, training is being imparted at affiliated and accredited training centres in 
various National Skills Qualification Framework (NSQF) aligned job roles including technology 
driven curriculum designed by Sector Skill Councils (SSCs) which are industry-led bodies. 
The present version of PMKVY i.e. PMKVY 3.0 has been designed as a demand-driven 
scheme with bottom-up approach for identification and mapping of job roles. Under Scheme, 
focus has been given for skilling on digital technology and Industry 4.0. The Sector Skill 
Councils (SSCs), which are autonomous industry-led bodies, have also created job roles on 
new and emerging digital technologies and industry 4.0 skills like Artificial Intelligence (AI) 
and Internet of Things (IoT). State-wise number of accredited and affiliated Training Centres 
including PMKK till date under PMKVY is given at column (b) of Annexure I-(A). 
 
MSDE through Directorate General of Training (DGT) is implementing CTS scheme to 
provide long term training through 14,711 Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) in 143 trades. 
State and sector wise details of ITIs are given at column (a) of Annexure I-(A)  and Annexure 
I-(B), respectively. Further, to meet skilling requirements arising out of changes and 
upgradation in technology, DGT has rolled out new-age courses. 
 
348

Additionally, Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) through 
National Manufacturing Competitiveness Programme (NMCP) is supporting MSMEs to 
develop global competitiveness. This program provides technological training through Tool 
Rooms (TRs) / Technology Centres (TCs). MSME in its endeavour to provide the right 
stimulus for the growth of the industry in the country – particularly with the objective of helping 
the micro, small and medium enterprises, has established 18 TRs/TCs all over in India. 
 
Out of these 18 TRs/TCs, 10 provide invaluable service to the Indian industry by way 
of precision tooling and providing well trained manpower in the area of tool and die making. 
The remaining 8 TRs/TCs are product specific centres to look into MSMEs specific problems 
and render technical services, developed & upgraded technologies and training in specific 
product groups like Foundry & Forging, Electronics, Electrical Measuring Instruments,

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
  
RAJYA SABHA 
  
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 915# 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 09.02.2022 
  
PROGRAMMES RUN BY NSDC FOR DIVYANG PERSONS 
  
915 #. SHRI NEERAJ DANGI: 
  
Will the Minister of SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP be pleased to state: 
  
(a)        the list of programmes being run by National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC) for 
Divyang persons; 
  
(b)        the number of job fairs by Government for these persons during the last three years; and 
  
(c)        the number of Divyang persons who benefitted under these schemes, the details thereof? 
  
ANSWER 
  
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE 
MINISTRY OF SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
(SHRI RAJEEV CHANDRASEKHAR) 
  
(a)        Under Skill India Mission, Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) is 
delivering skills to the youth of the country through its flagship scheme Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas 
Yojana (PMKVY). National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC) under the aegis of MSDE is 
implementing central component of Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) across the 
country covering all sections of society including Divyangjan (Persons with Disability (PwD)). As on 
31.12.2021, around 49,000 Divyangjans have been trained / oriented under PMKVY across the 
country. 
  
Under PMKVY, there are incentives to encourage participation of Divyangjan in the skill 
training, namely, monthly conveyance support; financial support for assistive devices, aid and 
appliances; and boarding and lodging. Also, an exclusive Sector Skill Council for Divyangjan known 
as Skill Council for PwD (SCPwD)  has been created for addressing the skilling needs of the 
Divyangjan. SCPwD empanels Divyangjan-friendly training centres, which are structurally designed to 
cover Braille, computer screen reader for visually impaired; sign language interpreter for speech and 
hearing impaired, etc. 
  
(b)        Job Fair/Rozgar Mela is a part of a placement outreach strategy to fast-track the interaction 
between employers and job seekers. Rozgar Melas are conducted by National Skill Development 
Corporation (NSDC), Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Kendras (PMKKs), Sector Skill Councils (SSCs) and 
Training Providers (TPs) as a part of overall “Placement incentives & Job Melas / Rozgar Utsav” 
component of PMKVY and it is an ongoing process. Rozgar Melas are conducted for all persons 
including Divyangjan. Special attention is given to the Divyangjan to provide them easier access to 
facilities such as registration windows for Divyangjan were made according to the needs. Also, 
specific group of employers are invited to the Rozgar Melas who are interested in hiring Divyangjan. 
As on 31.12.2021, 1576 Rojgar Melas have been conducted during the last three years. 
  
(c)        Above reply (a) may be referred to.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 916 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 09.02.2022 
  
OBJECTIVES AND STATUS OF PMKVY 
  
916 #  SHRI VINAY DINU TENDULKAR: 
  
Will the Minister of SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP be 
pleased to state: 
  
(a)       the objectives of Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) and the current 
status of implementation thereof; 
  
(b)       the State/Union Territory-wise details of the number of youth who have got 
employment under this scheme and the targets set under the said scheme including the 
number of potential beneficiaries marked for launching self employment enterprises, 
allocation and expenditure made thereon; and
 
  
(c)        the number of centres set up to train people belonging to various categories, 
including workers and persons who left studies midway in Goa under the said schemes?
 
  
ANSWER 
  
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE 
MINISTRY OF SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
(SHRI RAJEEV CHANDRASEKHAR) 
 
(a)       Under Skill India Mission, Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship 
(MSDE) is delivering skills through Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) with 
an objective to impart short duration skill development training and certification to youth 
and to make them employable for better livelihood across the country. Pradhan Mantri 
Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) was firstly launched in 2015. Presently, the third phase of 
PMKVY, i.e., PMKVY 3.0 (2020-22) is being implemented across the country. Since 
inception, till 31.12.2021, 1.34 crore candidates have benefited from the PMKVY across 
the country.
 
 
(b)       PMKVY has two training components, namely, Short Term Training (STT) and 
Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL). Under PMKVY, placement opportunities are being 
provided to STT certified candidates, while RPL is not linked with placements as it 
recognizes the existing skills of candidate. Under PMKVY-STT, 53.89 lakh candidates 
have been certified; out of which, 23.70 lakh candidates have been provided with the 
placement including 2.95 lakh self employed candidates in various sectors across the 
country. The State-wise details are given at Annexure I.
 
 
The phase-wise targets and candidates benefited under PMKVY since inception, as 
on 31.12.2021, is given below: 
                                                                                                         (No. in lakh) 
Phase Target Candidates Trained / Oriented 
PMKVY 1.0 (Phase I i.e. 2015-16) 24.00 19.86 
PMKVY 2.0 (Phase II i.e. 2016-20) 100.00 109.98 
PMKVY 3.0 (Phase III i.e. 2020-22) 8.00 4.45 
Total 132.00 lakh                                 134.29 lakh 
353

  
The PMKVY (except PMKVY 1.0 (2015-16)) has two components, namely, Central 
component being implemented through National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC), 
and State component being implemented through State Skill Development Mission of the 
State/UT. Under Central component of PMKVY, there is no provision of State-wise funds 
allocation. Since inception of the PMKVY, i.e., 2015, as on 31.12.2021, an amount of Rs. 
8,590.29 crore has been disbursed to implementing agency, i.e., NSDC towards the 
implementation of the scheme.
 
  
Under State component of PMKVY, funds and corresponding physical targets have 
been allocated to the States for the implementation of scheme through State Skill 
Development Missions (SSDMs). Since incorporation of State component, i.e., 2016, as 
on 31.12.2021, an amount of Rs. 1,224.82 crore has been disbursed to States for the 
implementation of the scheme. The State-wise funds allocated, disbursed and utilized by 
the State under PMKVY 2.0 and PMKVY 3.0, as on 31.12.2021, is given at Annexure II.
 
  
(c)        Under Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY), short term training is being 
implemented in accredited and affiliated training centres across the country. As on 
31.12.2021, short term training under PMKVY has been imparted through 44 training 
centres including Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Kendra in the State of Goa. 
 
  
Further, Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) promotes 
establishment of model training centres in every district of the country known as Pradhan 
Mantri Kaushal Kendra (PMKK). As on 15.01.2022, 2 PMKKs have been allocated in the 
State of Goa. Out of which, 1 PMKK has been established.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 917 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 09.02.2022 
  
PMKVY-THIRD PHASE 
 
917 SHRI T.G. VENKATESH: 
  
Will the Minister of SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP be 
pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether Government has contemplated on augmentation of implementation of 
third phase of PM Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) in the country; 
 
(
b) if so, the details thereof ; and 
 
(
c) the steps being taken by Government in this regard? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE 
MINISTRY OF SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
(SHRI RAJEEV CHANDRASEKHAR) 
 
(a) to (c) Ministry has launched a new version of Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas 
Yojana (PMKVY) i.e. PMKVY 3.0 (2020-21) on 15.01.2021 on the basis of the 
evaluation studies and learning from the implementation of PMKVY 1.0 and 2.0. Under 
PMKVY 3.0, the informed choices / aspirations of the candidates have been given 
primacy and it promotes candidates to opt for local skills with local jobs. Demand driven 
with bottom-up approach has been adopted under PMKVY 3.0. District Skill Committees 
(DSCs) are the focal point for implementation of PMKVY 3.0 at the district level. The 
DSCs are entrusted with district level skill gap and demand assessment, mobilization 
and counselling of candidates, formation of training batches, post training support and 
provide handholding support to the candidates after placements, besides addressing 
the grievances, if any. 
 
Despite disruption caused due to COVID-19 pandemic, 4.45 lakh candidates 
have been trained / oriented till 31.12.2021 under PMKVY 3.0 covering 711 districts of 
the country. The scheme has been extended till 31.03.2022.

UN-STARRED QUESTION NO: 918 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 09-02-2022 
AMENDING APPRENTICES ACT, 1961  
918 #  SHRI PRABHAKAR REDDY VEMIREDDY: 
Will the Minister of SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP be 
please to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that the ministry is planning to amend Apprentices Act, 1961 to 
allow training and educational institutions to hire apprentices and also provide training 
online; 
 
(b) if so, details of the proposal and how skill can be developed through online; 
 
(c) how proposed changes will help enlarge the scope of apprenticeship and 
availability of facilities in more and more areas; and 
 
(d) to what extent the proposed changes would increase apprentices in the country?  
 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY  
OF SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
(SHRI RAJEEV CHANDRASEKHAR) 
 
(a) to (d)  The Government is currently in the process of consultations with various 
stakeholders for improving the apprenticeship processes, guidelines and rules following 
which the draft amendment to the Apprentices Act, 1961 would be finalized. However, 
educational and training institutions are allowed to engage apprentices as per existing 
provisions of Apprentices Act, 1961. The ministry has simplified the guidelines for 
implementation of apprenticeship training which allows delivery of basic training through 
online mode, which may lead to increase in engagement of apprentices by the 
establishments in the country.

ITIs SET UP IN COUNTRY 
 
919:  SHRI VIJAY PAL SINGH TOMAR:

state:

country during the last three years as compared to the public sector;  
 
(b)  if so, the details of said institutes set up by the private as well as public sector ;  
 
(c)  whether Government monitors the quality of education and training in the said 
institutes; and  
 
(d)  if so, the details thereof? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF  
SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
(SHRI RAJEEV CHANDRASEKHAR) 
 
(a) Yes, Sir. 1115 private sector industrial Training Institutes (ITIS) have been set as 
compared to 942 public sector ITls in the country in the last three years.  
 
(b)  the state-wise details of private sector and public sector ITls set-up during the last 
three years are attached at Annexure-l. 
 
(c) and (d) Establishment and administration of ITls comes under the jurisdiction of State 
Government, while the policies such as setting the criterion for affiliation, conducting the 
examination along with certification and designing curriculum are the responsibilities of 
Central Government. Improving quality of training in ITIs is a continuous process. 
Towards this inter-alia standards and norms of affiliation are reviewed; curriculum & 
courses are revised as per industry practices, trainer / teacher recruitment is advocated 
and assessment practices are strengthened.  
 
For quality improvement, the State Governments carry out periodical Inspections 
and Joint Inspections in co-ordination with Union Government. To measure the quality of 
training imparted in ITls, the Union Government carries out periodical and timely gradings 
in the ITls under Skill Strengthening for Industrial Value Enhancement (STRIVE), and also 
426 ITls are supported for upgradation and quality addition.

(b) 23.7 lakh candidates have been provided employment under PMKVY since 
2015.1.02 lakh candidates have got self-employment/wage employment under JSS from 
2018-19 to 31.12.2021.SinceNAPS is an apprenticeship related scheme, no placement is

(c) Yes, Sir.  
(d) The Department of School Education & Literacy, Minis try of Education is 
implementing the component of Vocationalisation of School Education under the umbrella of 
Samagra Shiksha - an integrated scheme for school education', a Centrally Sponsored 
Scheme. The scheme aims at integrating Vocational Education with general academic 
education in all Secondary/Senior Secondary schools; enhancing the Employability and 
Entrepreneurial abilities of the students, providing exposure to work environment; and 
generating awareness amongst students about various career options so as to enable them 
to make a choice in accordance with their aptitude, competence and aspirations. The 
scheme covers Government and Government aided schools. 
Under Vocational Education component of *Samagra Shiksha*, NSQF compliant 
vocational courses are offered to the students from class 9th to 12th in the schools covered 
under the scheme. The State Governments have been advised that Vocational courses are 
to be treated at par with other academic subjects and accorded a similar status in the 
scheme of subjects. The States/UTs submit proposals as part of Annual Work Plan & 
Budget (AWP&B) which are considered by the Project Approval Board of Samagra Shiksha. 
 
Till March 2021, 12,813 schools have been approved under the scheme  out of which 
the scheme has so far been implemented in 11,710 schools with the reported enrolment of 
15,63,319 students. For the year 2021-22, 1622  new schools have been approved for 
Vocational Education under Samagra Shiksha taking the total number of schools approved 
for implementing the scheme to 14,435 schools. 
National Apprenticeship Training Scheme (NATS), Ministry of Education has been 
extended for the next five years with an outlay of Rs. 3,054 crore which will make, through 
apprenticeship, around 9 lakh students employable. Under the scheme students will be 
given apprenticeship in the emergingand frontier technology such as Artificial Intelligence, 
drone technology, new evolving and emergent areas including expertise required for 
Production Linked Incentive Scheme, and PM Gati Shakti Programme of the Government.  
362

As far as the Ministry of Skill Development & Entrepreneurship is concerned, it has 
recently signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Indira Gandhi Open University 
(IGNOU), the partnership aims to link vocational education and training with higher 
education, making India’s youth employable by creating avenues for them to access better 
work opportunities. The trainees attached to National Skill Training Institutes (NSTI), 
Industrial Training Institutes (ITI), Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Kendras (PMKK) and Jan 
Shikshan Sansthan (JSS) will benefit from the programme, aimed at creating upward 
mobility of these students to be able to attain higher education for better livelihood 
opportunities.  
Under the partnership, 32 NSTIs, more than 3,000 Government ITIs, 500 PMKKs and 
nearly 300 JSS will be associated with IGNOU as Registration Centres, Examination 
Centres and Work Centres for hands on training. Through the collaboration, students will 
now get an opportunity to join the three-year degree programme of IGNOU. There shall be a 
Project Steering Committee with representatives from both MSDE and IGNOU to monitor 
and review the progress of the programme. 
 The MoU is in alignment with the Sustainable Development Goal 4.4 and the 
National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 for increasing Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER) in higher 
education including vocational education to 50% by 2035.The Guidelines of Samagra 
Shiskha Abhiyan, B.Voc and Degree Apprenticeship has been finalized and published at the 
public domain. The Government is intending to provide short term market relevant courses 
to the formally educated students at centers under Ministry of Skill Development and 
Entrepreneurship.

(a)  the details of women entrepreneurship created/promoted by the implementation 
of the project named "Economic Empowerment of Women Entrepreneurs and Startups 
by Women" since 2020;  
 
(b)  the targets outlined by Government when the scheme was launched ;  
 
(c)  whether the above-mentioned targets have been achieved ;  
 
(d)  if so, the details thereof ; and  
 
(e)  if not, the reasons therefor?  
  
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF  
SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
(SHRI RAJEEV CHANDRASEKHAR) 
  
(a)       The project ‘ Economic Empowerment of Women Entrepreneurs and 
Startups by Women (WEE) ’ is being implemented by the Ministry of Skill 
Development and Entrepreneurship in collaboration with Deutsche Gesellschaftfür 
Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) Germany on behalf of the German Federal 
Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ).  
 
The project aims to pilot incubation and acceleration programmes for women 
micro entrepreneurs, enabling them to start new businesses and scale up existing 
enterprises in the States of Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Telangana, Uttar Pradesh and 8 
North Eastern States of the country. 
 
Under the title of ‘Her&Now’, the project envisages a film and media campaign 
to tell the stories of successful women entrepreneurs and to foster a positive mindset 
change on gender roles and expand women entrepreneurship. 
  
(b)  The project targets to support 315 aspiring women entrepreneurs, from the 
selected states, to turn their ideas into a business in the seven-month incubation 
programme. During the six-month acceleration programme, 130 women with existing 
businesses were targeted to support to grow their enterprises.

against the targeted 445 women under both incubation and acceleration support 
programmes.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 927 
   TO BE ANSWERED ON 09.02.2022 
 
SAFETY AND WELFARE OF DIVYANGJANS DURING COVID-19 
927.  SHRI SYED NASIR HUSSAIN: 
Will the Minister of Social Justice and Empowerment be pleased to state: 
 
 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR SOCIAL JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT 
(SUSHRI PRATIMA BHOUMIK) 
(a) and (b) On 26.03.2020, the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities issued 
‘Comprehensive Disability Inclusive Guidelines for protection and safety of persons with disabilities 
(Divyangjan) during COVID 19’ to all States/UTs. These guidelines inter-alia provides that caregivers 
of persons with disabilities (PwDs) should be allowed to reach the divyangjan by exempting them from 
restrictions during lockdown or providing passes in a simplified manner on priority. These guidelines 
mandate the State Commissioner for PwDs and the District officer dealing with empowerment of PwDs 
to act as the State Nodal authority and the District Nodal authority respectively to resolve disability 
specific issues of PwDs. 
  
    Data regarding number of passes issued to caregivers is not maintained in the Ministry. 
(a) whether any special passes have been issued in the past one year to allow unobstructed travel of 
caregivers of persons with disabilities (PwDs) during lockdown situations as per the 
“Comprehensive Disability Inclusive Guidelines for protection and safety of persons with 
disabilities (Divyangjan) during COVID-19”, issued by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare 
in 2020;  
(b) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor; and 
(c) the details of all measures undertaken for the protection of PwDs from the COVID-19 pandemic? 
384

 
(c)    Apart from issuing ‘Comprehensive Disability Inclusive Guidelines for protection and safety of 
persons with disabilities (Divyangjan) during COVID 19’ stated above, the following measures have also 
been taken :- 
  
      On 24.04.2020, all the States/UTs have been requested by the Ministry to ensure barrier free 
environment and easy access to persons with benchmark disabilities in the centres for COVID- 19 testing 
& quarantine facilities as well as for treatment at hospitals & health centres. 
  
      Keeping in view the need to address mental health concerns during COVID 19, the Department 
launched a dedicated 24x7 toll free Mental Health Rehabilitation helpline service ‘KIRAN’on 7th 
September, 2020. 
  
      The Ministry developed a Standard Operating Procedure (SoP) during Covid- 19 pandemic, with a 
view to ensuring  assessment of persons with disabilities and distribution of aids and assistive devices to 
them, by maintaining social distancing and adhering to sanitization protocols. 
  
       The Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT) issued Circulars, from time to time, allowing 
employees with disabilities to work from home. 
  
       
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare issued a guidance note on 14.04.2020 to all States/UTs to 
address health concern of all citizens including persons with disabilities to avail uninterrupted emergency 
health care services. They also issued guidel ines to all States/UTs on ‘Near to Home COVID 
Vaccination Centres (NHCVC)’ for elderly and persons with disabilities (PwDs) in May 2021, thereby 
making the vaccination program more accessible to them. Further, States/UTs were issued advisory 
regarding facilities to be provided to PwDs for COVID- 19 at treatment, management and vaccination 
centres besides prioritizing vaccination for PwDs. 
  
       The Ministry of Rural Development has informed that during COVID- 19 induced lockdown, Rs. 80 
crore was released to the States/UTs under Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Yojna (PMGKYP) for payment 
of ex-gratia of Rs. 1000/- in two installments (Rs. 500 each) to 8 lakh existing beneficiaries of Indira 
Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme (IGNDPS).

WELFARE SCHEMES FOR DIFFERENTLY-ABLED PERSONS 
  
  
930.  SMT. VANDANA CHAVAN: 
  
Will the Minister of Social Justice and Empowerment be pleased to state: 
  
(a) whether Government has undertaken any national survey of accessibility of essential public spaces 
– transport, health facilities and schools, and if so, the details thereof; 
  
(b) the percentage of such public spaces found to be accessible, the details thereof; 
  
(c) the targets set for Accessible India Campaign in 2015 and the progress thereof; and 
  
(d) the State/UT/year-wise details of amount spent on upgrading sports infrastructure for the 
differently-abled? 
  
ANSWER 
  
MINISTER OF STATE FOR SOCIAL JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT 
(SUSHRI PRATIMA BHOUMIK) 
  
(a) and (b)  : Under the Accessible India Campaign (AIC), access audits of 1671 selected State/UT 
Government buildings have been conducted in the year 2016-17 through empanelled auditors of the 
Ministry. The buildings included essential public spaces – transport, health facilities and schools, 
among others.  As on 31.01.2022, out of 1671 buildings identified during access audit, this Ministry 
has provided support to State/UT Governments to make 1191 buildings accessible under AIC. 20 
State/UT Governments have reported that they have so far made 577 buildings accessible (48.5%). 
The details of State-wise buildings reported to have been made accessible is given at Annexure A. 
  
(c): The details of targets and status of progress made under the Accessible India Campaign are given 
at Annexure B. 
  
(d): The Ministry provides financial assistance to  Central Government Departments and State/UT 
Governments for making sports infrastructure accessible to the persons with disabilities under the 
Scheme “Scheme for Implementation of Rights of persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 (SIPDA)”. 
  Under AIC, approximately Rs. 2.5 crore has been provided for 6  sports facilities in 4 States 
(Maharashtra, Mizoram, Haryana, Nagaland). Under the Creation of Barrier Free Environment, which 
is a sub-scheme under SIPDA Scheme, Rs. 12.41 crore has been provided to Sports Authority of India 
for 6 facilities in 4 States (Karnataka, Kerala, Punjab, Gujarat).The Department has also released Rs 
34 crore to CPWD for construction of Centre for Disability Sports at Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh.

Ministry gives approval to the State after a proposal is received from the State for setting 
up a EMRS which fulfills criteria of 20000 tribal population and 50% tribals in that 
block.  Formal sanction letter is issued by NESTS when the state sends Land suitability 
report and certifies availability of land free from all encumbrances. The construction 
agency is asked to prepare a Master Lay out and Detailed project report.   After due 
verification, the approval is given to go ahead with the tender process and start 
construction. A period of 18 months is provided for completion of construction.   It is 
expected that the entire process from giving formal sanction to completion of construction 
would take 24 months.  However due to covid lock-down, there has been delays in 
completion of the projects at some places.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF TRIBAL AFFAIRS 
RAJYA SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO- 934 
TO BE ANSWERED ON- 09/02/2022 
  
MARKET SUPPORT FOR TRIBAL PRODUCE 
  
934.  SHRI K.J. ALPHONS: 
  
Will the Minister of TRIBAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state:  
(a) the support that has been provided by Government during the last five years for the marketing 
of tribal produce; 
(b) the items of minor forest produce for which support price is being provided; and 
(c) whether it has made the life of these tribal communities self-sustaining? 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR TRIBAL AFFAIRS 
(SMT. RENUKA SINGH SARUTA) 
(a) Ministry of Tribal Affairs (MoTA) has taken various initiatives to facilitate marketing of tribal 
produce and the products made by the tribal people, which include the following: 
(i) The Ministry provides funds to States and Tribal Co-Operative Marketing Development 
Federation of India (TRIFED) for organizing tribal festivals wherein the tribal artists and artisans 
showcase and sell their products.  The details of National Tribal festival (Adi-Mahotsav), State level 
Adi Mahotsav organized by TRIFED and funds given to different State Governments for organizing 
such festivals is given in Annexure 1. 
These festivals and exhibitions showcase their traditional skill in painting, art and craft, organic 
products and also demonstrate glimpses of rich cultural heritage through unique forms of folk 
dances, songs, cuisine,. Due to Covid, pandemic during 2020-21and 2021-22, States and TRIFED 
were advised to organize such festival(s) after following Covid protocol and avail the use of digital 
platforms.  
(ii) MoTA provides funds to TRIFED and State Governments for marketing of tribal products by 
empaneling tribal suppliers comprising of individual tribal artisans, tribal SHGs, Organisations/ 
Agencies/NGOs working with the tribals. 
(iii) TRIFED also organizes Tribal Artisan Mela (TAM) at District/Tehsil level as an exercise to reach 
tribals located in interior areas and source tribal art and craft directly from them. Through this 
initiative, Tribal Artisans are invited to an exhibition area where they display their artifacts. 
(iv) TRIFED is also engaged in direct purchase and sale of tribal products including artifacts through 
its network of Tribes India Showrooms, exhibitions, Aadi Mahotsav, online e-commerce portal etc. 
The amount utilized in the last five years for purchase of tribal products is at Annexure 2. 
 
415

 
(b) The list of minor forest produce for which minimum support price is provided under the scheme 
‘Marketing of Minor Forest Produce (MFP) Through Minimum Support Price (MSP) And 
Development of Value Chain For MFP’ is at Annexure 3. 
(c) The Ministry of Tribal Affairs in coordination with State Government always strives for livelihood 
driven sustainable tribal development. The approach  is aimed at developing or growing by using 
resources in a way that allows for them to renew or continue to exist for others and protecting the 
environment.   As part of this continuing endeavor, cabinet has approved Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya 
Vikas Mission for the XV Finance Commission cycle.   The Mission seeks to achieve livelihood 
driven tribal development in the next five years through formation of Vandhan groups who have 
been organized into Vandhan Kendras.  The MFP gathered by tribals will be processed in these 
kendras and marketed through  Van Dhan Producer Enterprises.  New haats bazaar and ware 
houses will be developed in next 5 years as part of “Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhyan”.  TRIFED would 
be the nodal agency for implementing the scheme. The products produced will be marketed through 
Tribe India Stores. An amount of Rs. 1612 cr has been earmarked under the Mission for next five 
years. In the budget, an amount of Rs. 499 cr. has been earmarked under the mission.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF TRIBAL AFFAIRS 
RAJYA SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO- 935 
TO BE ANSWERED ON- 09/02/2022 
  
DISPLACEMENT OF TRIBALS 
  
935. SHRI AKHILESH PRASAD SINGH: 
  
Will the Minister of TRIBAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) Whether it is a fact that large number of tribal families across various States have been displaced 
due to Left-Wing Extremism; 
(b)  If so, how many such families have been displaced in the last three years and whether any data 
pertaining to such displaced tribal families is maintained by the Ministry; and 
(c) whether the Ministry has any scheme for rehabilitating the tribals displaced because of Left 
Wing Extremism, if so, details thereof? 
  
  
  
ANSWER 
  
MINISTER OF STATE FOR TRIBAL AFFAIRS 
(SHRI BISHWESWAR TUDU)  
 (a) to (c): Ministry of Tribal Affairs does not maintain data about movement of tribal families due 
to local disturbances.  However, as informed by Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), to address the 
left-wing extremism holistically, a National Policy & Action Plan was promulgated in 2015. The 
Development is one of the most important prong of the Policy. Following the Policy, several 
development schemes are being implemented specifically in the Left-Wing Extremism (LWE) 
affected areas in addition to the flagship schemes of Government of India. Special thrust is on 
expansion of road network, improvement in telecom connectivity, education, skill development and 
financial inclusion. 
Few of the specific interventions for LWE affected areas through various Ministries are as under:  
 
i. Special Central Assistance (SCA) for the most LWE affected Districts: Govt. of India has 
approved this scheme in 2017, under this scheme funds are given by MHA to the Most LWE 
Affected District to fill critical gaps in public infrastructure and services, which are of emergent 
nature and require immediate action. Till now, Rs.3078 crore has been released to the States. 
 
 
 
425

ii. Road Requirement  Plan-1(RRP-1) for LWE affected areas  :This Scheme is being 
implemented through Ministry of Road Transport and Highways since February, 2009 for 
improving road connectivity in 34 most LWE districts. 5361 km roads was sanctioned under the 
scheme ,out of which 5019 km have been completed with an expenditure of Rs. 7964 crore. 
iii. Road Connectivity Project for LWE affected Areas(RCPLWEA): This Scheme is being 
implemented through Ministry of Rural Development since 2016-17 with an outlay of Rs.11,725 
crore.10,231 km (1030 road & 463 bridges)was sanctioned till date, out of which 5160 km length 
(335 roads & 130 bridges) have been completed. 
iv. Mobile Connectivity project in LWE affected districts : The Scheme is being implemented 
through Department of Telecommunications. In phase-1, 2343 mobile tower shave been installed 
with a coast of Rs. 4080.78 crore. In phase-II, work has been issued of 2542 mobile towers. 
v. Skill Development Scheme in 47 district affected by LWE . The Scheme is being implemented 
by Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship since 2011. 47 ITIs and 68 SDCs have 
been approved with an estimated cost of Rs.407.85 crore.43 ITIs and 37 SDCs are functional. 
 Further, Government is implementing Tribal Sub-Plan (TSP)/Schedule Tribe Component  
(STC)/Development Action Plan for Development of STs (DAPST) for overall development of 
tribal people across the country. Besides, Ministry of Tribal Affairs, 40 Central Ministries / 
Departments have been obligated by NITI Aayog for earmarking certain percentage of their total 
Scheme allocation every year as STC funds for tribal development. STC funds are spent by 
different Central Ministries / Departments under their schemes for various development projects 
relating to education, health, agriculture, irrigation, roads, housing, drinking water, electrification, 
employment generation, skill development, etc., for accelerated socio-economic development of 
Scheduled Tribes. In addition, Ministry of Tribal Affairs provides funds under its schemes to 
supplement the efforts of tribal development by other Ministries/Departments.

   GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
         MINISTRY OF TRIBAL AFFAIRS 
RAJYA SABHA 
            UNSTARRED No- 936 
        TO BE ANSWERED ON- 09/02/2022 
  
PROJECT MONITORING UNITS FOR TRIBAL WELFARE SCHEMES 
  
936. SHRI SHAMSHER SINGH DULLO: 
SMT. PHULO DEVI NETAM: 
SHRI ANAND SHARMA: 
  
Will the Minister of TRIBAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state? 
  
(a) whether any central project monitoring units have been set up in States to oversee 
the implementation of tribal welfare schemes as announced by the Government in 
November 2021; 
(b) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor;  
(c)  the status of allocation, disbursal and utilisation of fund toward this initiative, as on 
date, for both Central and State units; 
(d) whether Government has set deadlines for the Central and State monitoring units to 
be functional; and 
(e)  if so, the details thereof and if not, the reason therefor?  
  
  
  
ANSWER 
  
MINISTER OF STATE FOR TRIBAL AFFAIRS 
(SMT. RENUKA SINGH SARUTA)                 
  
(a) to (e):  The Ministry of Tribal Affairs implements various Central Sector and Centrally 
Sponsored Scheme through States /UT Government.  Ministry in last few years has undergone 
a major strategic shift and has developed scheme specific portals with end to end digitization 
of various processes ensuring physical and financial monitoring of the funds released under 
different schemes. 
  
Ministry is not aware about specific announcement of the Government for setting up of PMUs 
in states.  However, the NITI Aayog has initiated Data Governance Quality Index which 
evaluates various Ministries on data-based Governance and has advised all Ministries to set up 
Data and Strategy units in Ministry for digitization of processes related to implementation and 
monitoring of Central Sector/Centrally sponsored schemes of Ministries/Departments. 
  
Till 14th Finance Cycle (from 2016-17 to 2020-21), amount ranging from 1-2% of the scheme 
was given to States/UTs as administrative cost for implementation of the Schemes. While 
approving the continuation of Centrally Sponsored and Central Sector Scheme for 
Development of STs over the 15th Finance Commission (2021-22 to 2025-26), funds have been 
provided to set up State Programme Management Unit (SPMU) at State level for effective 
implementation and monitoring of the combined schemes of the Ministry.  Funds have also 
been earmarked under the scheme "Monitoring, Evaluation, Survey and Social Audit" 
including setting up of Central PMU.  The role of central PMU is to co- ordinate with the State 
units for providing data in respect of various schemes.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA

TO BE ANSWERED ON- 09/02/2022 
  
POPULATION TREND OF PVTGs IN INDIA 
  
937.  SHRI MAHESH PODDAR: 
  
Will the Minister of TRIBAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
  
(a) the population trend of the Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) in India in the last 
three years along with the latest population figure, the details thereof, tribe-wise; 
(b) the status of such tribal population in Jharkhand and the measures that have been taken by 
Government to increase their population; and 
(c) the amount dedicated for the tribal development projects and how much has been utilized till 
date? 
  
  
  
ANSWER 
  
MINISTER OF STATE FOR TRIBAL AFFAIRS 
(SHRI BISHWESWAR TUDU) 
  
(a) & (b):   At present, there are 75 Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) spread across 
18 States and the Union Territory of Andaman & Nicobar Islands in the country. As per 
information received from the Office of Registrar General & Census Commissioner, Registrar 
General of India (RGI), no data on Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) is collected in 
Census and only those tribes are enumerated separately which are specifically notified as 
Scheduled Tribes (STs) as per Presidential Order under the Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) 
Order, 1950 amended from time to time. As the enumeration of tribes other than STs has not 
been done separately in any of the decadal Censuses since 1951 Census, the population figure/ 
trend for the PVTGs communities as a whole is not available centrally. Also, since the population 
figures are not collected annually, the population trend for last three years is not 
available.   Information, as provided by the Office of Registrar General of India, on the State-
wise decadal population for PVTGs is given in Annexure -I. 
  
 (c):  With the objective of bringing about overall socio-economic development and welfare of the 
most vulnerable sections among tribals who are classified as the Particularly Vulnerable Tribal 
Groups (PVTGs), the Government has extended financial assistance under the “Scheme of 
Development of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs)” to the PVTG concentrated 
States/UT based on their proposals for development of PVTG communities in the sectors such 
as education, housing, land development, agricultural development, animal husbandry, 
construction of link roads, installation of non-conventional sources of energy for lighting purpose, 
social security or any other innovative activity meant for the comprehensive socio-economic 
development of PVTGs and to fill in the critical gaps in development. The scheme is implemented 
in accordance with Conservation-Cum- Development (CCD) Plans prepared by the State /UT 
Governments and projects/ activities taken up under this scheme are demand driven. These 
communities are also expected to be covered under other schemes of Government of India (i) 
428

which are directed towards all eligible persons, (ii) are targeted towards the tribal populations 
under the various schemes of the Central and State Governments  under the Scheduled Tribe 
component as well as (iii) the major schemes targeted at the tribal population of the Ministry of 
Tribal Affairs and the Departments concerned with the development and welfare of tribal 
populations in the State Governments. 
  
 
         Details of funds released to the State Governments and utilization thereof under the

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF TRIBAL AFFAIRS 
RAJYA SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No- 938 
TO BE ANSWERED ON- 09/02/2022 
  
PROTECTING HABITATION OF TRIBALS  
  
938. SHRI N. R. ELANGO:  
  
Will the Minister of TRIBAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
  
(a) the steps taken to protect the habitation of tribals; and 
(b) the steps taken to document, improve and augment income for the tribals from their natural 
skills? 
  
  
 ANSWER 
  
  
MINISTER OF STATE FOR TRIBAL AFFAIRS 
(SHRI BISHWESHWAR TUDU) 
  
(a):  Ministry of Tribal Affairs administers “The Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest 
Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006” (FRA in short), which was passed by the 
Parliament in 2006. The Act was notified for its operation on 31.12.2007 and rules thereunder 
were notified on 01.01.2008, as amended in 2012. 
  
FRA is an Act to recognize and vest the forest rights and occupation in forest land in forest 
dwelling Scheduled Tribes and other traditional forest dwellers who have been residing in such 
forests for generations but whose rights could not be recorded; to provide for a framework for 
recording the forest rights so vested and the nature of evidence required for such recognition 
and vesting in respect of forest land. 
  
Section 3(1)(a) of FRA provides the right to hold and live in the forest land under the individual 
or common occupation for habitation or for self-cultivation for livelihood by a member or 
members of a forest dwelling Scheduled Tribe or other traditional forest dwellers; 
  
Section 3(1)(e) of FRA provides the rights including community tenures of habitat and habitation 
for primitive tribal groups and pre-agricultural communities. 
  
As per the Act and Rules, State Governments are responsible for implementation of various 
provisions of the Act. 
  
 
 
 
 
 
433

 
 
 
(b): The Ministry of Tribal Affairs implements the following income generation schemes for tribal 
population keeping in view the traditional skills of the tribals:  
 
  
1. Institutional Support for Development and Marketing of Tribal Products & Produce 
 
Under the scheme, Grants-in-aid are released to State Tribal Development Cooperative 
Corporations (STDCCs) and Tribal Cooperative Marketing Development Federation of India Ltd. 
(TRIFED). The objective of the Scheme is to create institutions for the Scheduled Tribes to 
support marketing and development of activities they depend on for their livelihood by: 
 
i. Market intervention, 
ii. Training and skill up-gradation of Tribal Artisans, Craftsmen, Minor Forest Produce (MFP) 
gatherers 
iii. Research & Development (R&D) / Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) activities, and 
iv. Supply chain infrastructure development. 
 
 
2. Marketing of Minor Forest Produce (MFP) Through Minimum Support Price (MSP) And 
Development of Value Chain For MFP” 
  
The scheme seeks to establish a system to ensure fair monetary returns for their efforts in 
collection, primary processing, storage, packaging, transportation etc. It also seeks to get them 
a share of revenue from the sales proceeds with cost deducted. It also aims to address other 
issues for sustainability of process. The scheme envisages fixation and declaration of Minimum 
Support Price for the selected MFP. Procurement & Marketing operation at prefixed MSP will be 
undertaken by the designated State Agencies. Simultaneously, other medium- &long-term 
issues like sustainable collection, value addition, infrastructure development, knowledge base 
expansion of MFP, market intelligence development, strengthening the bargaining power of 
Gram Sabha/ Panchayat are also addressed.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO- 939 
TO BE ANSWERED ON- 09/02/2022 
 
 WELFARE MEASURES FOR TRIBAL MIGRANT FAMILIES 
 
939. SHRI PARTAP SINGH BAJWA: 
  
Will the Minister of TRIBAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
  
(a) the details of schemes and welfare measures launched by the Ministry for tribal migrant 
families till date; 
 
(b) the State-wise details on the number of tribal migrant families covered under the scheme, till 
date; 
 
(c) the State-wise details on occupation and employment rate of tribal migrant families till date; 
and 
 
(d) the State-wise details on migration trend from origin to place of migration of tribal migrant 
families till date? 
ANSWER 
  
MINISTER OF STATE FOR TRIBAL AFFAIRS 
(SMT. RENUKA SINGH SARUTA) 
 
(a) to (d) Under the STC framework, 41 Central Ministries are required to allocate funds for the 
welfare of STs and development of tribal areas through over 260 different schemes for 
development projects relating to education, health, agriculture, irrigation, roads, housing, 
electrification, employment generation, skill development, aimed at their sustainable 
development.  An amount of Rs. 87,584 has been allocated in 2022 as Schedule Tribe Component 
as against an amount of Rs. 78,256 in the previous year.  
  
Ministry of Labour ,the nodal Ministry mandated with migration issues has informed that the 
Government has enacted Inter-State Migrant Workmen (Regulation of Employment and 
Conditions of Service) Act, 1979 which has been subsumed into Occupational Safety, Health and 
Working Conditions (OSH) Code, 2020. Further, the Code on Wages, 2019, Occupational Safety, 
Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020, Code on Social Security, 2020 and the Industrial 
Relations Code, 2020 provide for decent working conditions, minimum wages and social security 
benefits to all category of workers including migrant workers. Special provision such as widening 
the definition of Inter-state migrant workers, toll free helpline, journey allowance, etc for migrant 
workers have been incorporated in the OSH Code, 2020. 
 
 
435

The Unorganized Workers’ Social Security Act, 2008, now subsumed in the Code on Social 
Security, 2020, provides for social security to all unorganized workers including migrant workers. 
Government has launched various social security schemes like Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Beema 
Yojana (PMJJBY) and Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Beema Yojana (PMSBY) for life and disability 
cover and Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Man Dhan  Pension Yojana (PM-SYM) in March, 2019 for 
pension to the unorganised workers including migrant workers. Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri 
Jan Arogya Yojana (PMJAY) launched in 2018 provides Rs.5 lakh health coverage for secondary 
and tertiary health benefits to all unorganized workers including migrant workers who are covered 
as eligible beneficiaries as per Socio Economic Caste census Data, 2011.  
 The Ministry of Labour & Employment, has developed e-shram portal for registration and creation 
of a comprehensive National Database of Unorganized Workers (NDUW) such as construction 
workers , Migrant Workers, Domestic Workers, Agricultural labourers, Self-employed workers, 
street vendors, small shopkeepers, Asha workers, Anganwadi workers, Fishermen, unorganised 
plantation workers, milkmen and similar other sub-group of Unorganised workers. The e-Shram 
Portal was  launched on 26.08.2021 and handed over to the States/UTs.  The portal will work as a 
useful platform for delivery of existing and future social security schemes such as PM-SBY, PM-
SYM etc. Till date, 25,15,85,944 persons have registered on on e-Shram portal, out of which 
1,91,41,085 are tribals which is 7.61% of the total registration. The State-wise list of STs registered 
on the portal as on 06.02.2022 is given in the Annexure. 
 
 
  
As tribals have been traditionally dependent on forest for their livelihood, Ministry of Tribal 
Affairs has launched Pradhan Mantri Janjatiye Vikkas Mission to achieve livelihood driven tribal 
development  for the next Finance Commission Cycle and an amount of Rs. 1612 cr has been 
earmarked under the Mission.  Likewise  National Scheduled Tribes Finance and Development 
Corporation (NSTFDC) under the ministry provides financial assistance at concessional rate of 
interest for improving their productivity. Various other scheme of the mInistry like Marketing of 
Minor Forest Produce (MFP) through Minimum Support Price (MSP)”,   “Special Central 
Assistance to Tribal Sub-Scheme (SCA to TSS)” and “Grants under Article 275 (1) of the 
Constitution of India”are additive to state plan funds and efforts for tribal development through 
substantial reduction in poverty and unemployment, creation of productive assets and income 
generating opportunities.  
  
Through various other schemes like Under Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyan 
(PMGKRA), Aatmanirbhar Bharat Rozgar Yojna (ABRY), • Mahatma Gandhi National Rural 
Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA),  PM Garib Kalyan Ann Yojana , Pradhan Mantri Jan 
DhanYojana (PMJDY),  PM KISAN Yojana , Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana 
(PMKVY)and initiatives have been taken to boost rural infrastructure and rural economy to 
provide local employment opportunities particularly to the migrant returnees.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO- 940 
TO BE ANSWERED ON- 09/02/2022 
  
ESTABLISHMENT OF EMRS 
940.  SHRI DEREK O' BRIEN:  
Will the Minister of TRIBAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) the budget allocation for establishing Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS) in 
the last five years, the details thereof; 
(b) the percentage of the budget allocated in 2021-22 which has been utilised so far, the 
details thereof; 
(c) whether the target of establishing 462 new Eklavya schools has been achieved; and 
(d) if not, in how many sub districts are Eklavya schools yet to be built? 
  
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR TRIBAL AFFAIRS 
(SMT. RENUKA SINGH SARUTA) 
  
(a) and (b):  Till the year 2019-20, funds for the construction of EMRS and day to day 
recurring expenses were being released under Article 275(1) of the Constitution. After the 
scheme of EMRS was approved as a separate scheme by the cabinet, funds under the 
scheme are released by this Ministry to National Education Society for Tribal Students 
(NESTS) for further disbursement to various State/UT societies for running and 
maintenance of EMRSs and CPWD/PSUs/States for construction/upgradation of EMRSs 
across the country.  
Cabinet has recently approved an amount of Rs 38 cr and 48 crore as against Rs. 20 cr 
and 24 crore in plain and hilly/NE/LWE areas respectively for construction of new EMRSs 
being constructed.  Funds are released @ Rs. 1.09 lakh per student/annum towards 
recurring expenses.  
 The fund released towards Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS) in the last five 
years and current year (as on 3.2.2022) are given as under.  
 
        (Rs. in Lakh) 
  FY 2016-17 FY 2017-18 FY 2018-19 FY 2019-20 FY 2020-21 
Fund released 126581.37 150939.89 181498.70 266140.83 119997.88 
 
 
438

 
 
 
Note:- upto the year 2019-20, the release figure includes EMRS and other activities under 
Article 275(1). 
During the current year 2021-22 an amount of Rs. 86648.00 lakhs has so far been 
released to NESTS against the RE allocation of 105774.00 lakh which is around 82% of 
RE allocation.  
(c) and (d): Government has decided to establish 740 EMRSs across the country in blocks 
having more than 50% tribal population and at least 20,000 tribal persons. Out of these 
740, 288 are old schools [sanctioned under Article 275(1) of the Constitution], whereas 
452 schools are to be established as per new scheme. Under new scheme, Ministry has 
so far approved EMRSs at 377 locations.  Formal sanction letter is issued by NESTS 
when the state sends Land suitability report and certifies availability of land free from all 
encumbrances. The construction agency is asked to prepare a Master Lay out and 
Detailed project report.   After due verification, the approval is given to go ahead with the 
tender process and start construction. A period of 18 months is provided for completion 
of construction.   It is expected that the entire process from giving formal sanction to 
completion of construction would take 24 months.  However due to covid lock-down, there 
has been delays in completion of the projects at some places.   Ministry has fixed target 
of construction of all schools by 2025.

these cases are at Annexure.

'ONE-STOP CENTRE' SCHEME IN TAMIL NADU 
  
943 :    SHRI M. MOHAMED ABDULLA: 
  
Will the Minister of WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
  
(a)  the total number of women assisted through the 'One-Stop Centre' scheme, 
district-wise for the State of Tamil Nadu from the year 2017; 
(b)   the schemes implemented by the District Level Centre for Women(DLCW) 
associated with Mahila Shakti Kendra (MSK) and the total number of 
beneficiaries, district-wise for the State of Tamil Nadu during the last five years; 
and 
(c)  the amount of funds allocated, disbursed and utilised for the schemes of the 
Ministry for the State of Tamil Nadu, district-wise during the last five years? 
  
ANSWER 
  
MINISTER OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT  
(SHRIMATI SMRITI ZUBIN IRANI) 
  
(a):  The Central Government implements the One Stop Centre (OSC) Scheme with 
effect from 1st April, 2015 to provide integrated support and assistance to women 
aﬀected by violence and in distress, both in private and public spaces, through a range 
of services including police facilitation, medical aid, legal aid and counseling, 
psychological support and temporary shelter in an integrated manner under one roof. 
As of now, 733 OSCs have been approved, out of which 704 have been 
operationalized in 35 States/ UTs (in Tamil Nadu, 34 OSCs are operational), which 
have assisted over 4.50 lakh women in the country till September, 2021. The total 
number of women assisted through the OSC scheme, district-wise, in Tamil Nadu from 
the year 2017 is at Annexure - I.  
  
(b) : The District Level Centre for Women (DLCW) in Tamil Nadu undertook activities 
for creating awareness among women about various policies, programmes and 
schemes pertaining to women. There is no provision for monetary benefit directly to 
any beneficiary under the scheme.

IMPORTANCE OF AADHAR IN ANGANWADI SERVICES       
  
945:  SHRI K C VENUGOPAL: 
  
Will the Minister of WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:  
  
(a) whether it is a fact that there is excessive Aadhaar imposition and Aadhaar is 
routinely demanded from children for basic rights such as Anganwadi services or 
school enrolment; 
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; 
(c) whether it is also fact that for female adult, alternatives to Aadhaar are  often lack
ing and this has happened even for COVID-19 vaccination; and 
(d) if so, the steps taken by Government so that the benefits paid from the Consolida
ted Fund of India could be provided even if Aadhaar fails? 
  
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF  WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRIMATI SMRITI ZUBIN IRANI) 
  
(a) & (b).        The beneficiaries under the Anganwadi Services are identified on the 
basis of Aadhar which is used as identity document for delivery of services or benefits 
which brings in transparency and efficiency and enables beneficiaries to get their 
entitlements.The beneficiaries not possessing Aadhaar card are assisted by the field 
functionaries to obtain the Aadhaar card. Till such time, they are provided the services 
on the basis of alternative identification document.  
  
(c)   Following type of Photo ID cards have been allowed by Government of India for 
availing Covid-19 vaccination at all covid vaccination centers, to ensure that a large 
basket of photo identity proofs are available for people to avail Covid-19 vaccination. 
Following Nine Photo Identity Documents can be used by citizens above 18 years of 
age for registration on Cowin portal. 
 
a. Aadhaar Card  
b. Driving License  
c. PAN Card 
d. Passport  
e. Pension Passbook  
f. NPR Smart Card  
g. Voter ID (EPIC)  
h. Unique Disability Identification Card (UDIC) 
i. Ration Card with Photo  
447

Following 6 Photo Identity documents can be used by citizens 15-18 years of age for 
registration on Cowin Portal:  
 
a. Aadhaar Card  
b. PAN Card  
c. Passport  
d. Unique Disability Identification Card (UDIC)  
e. Ration Card with Photo 
 f. Student Photo ID card  
 
Under National COVID- l9 Vaccination Programme, there is provision to facilitate 
vaccination of persons without prescribed identity cards (including Aadhar Card) 
through special sessions where 100% vaccination is done through on-site registration 
by the vaccinator under a special procedure. Government of India has shared a 
Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) regarding 'COVID19 Vaccination of Persons 
without Prescribed Identity Cards through Co-WIN' with all States/UTs in May 2021. 
 
As on 4thFebruary, 2022, 48.78% of the total doses were administered to women which 
approximates to the estimated proportion of women in the country's population which is 
48%. 
 
(d)      Services are provided to the beneficiaries on the basis of alternative identification 
document, even if they are not possessing Aadhar Card.

UN-STARRED QUESTION NO. 946 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 09.02.2022   
  
RISE IN CHILD MARRIAGE 
  
946 :    PROF. MANOJ KUMAR JHA: 
  
Will the Minister of WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
  
(a)  the measures taken by Government to prevent the rise of child marriages during 
the pandemic; 
(b)   the number of awareness campaigns undertaken by Government to specifically 
deal with the problem, State-wise; and 
(c)   the details of activities and programmes the National Commission for Protection 
of Child Rights (NCPCR) has undertaken to prevent child marriages, State-wise? 
  
ANSWER 
  
MINISTER OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT  
(SHRIMATI SMRITI ZUBIN IRANI) 
  
  
(a) & (b) : The Government has enacted the ‘Prohibition of Child Marriage Act (PCMA), 
2006’ for prohibition of solemnisation of child marriages and for matters connected 
therewith or incidental thereto. Section 16 of the PCMA Act authorises the State 
Government to appoint for the whole State, or such part thereof as may be specified, an 
officer or officers to be known as the 'Child Marriage Prohibition Officers (CMPO)' 
having jurisdiction over the area or areas specified in the notification. The Section also 
specifies the functions to be discharged by CMPOs, which also includes creation of 
awareness about the detrimental effects of child marriages and to sensitize the 
community about this issues. These authorities function under the superintendence of 
respective State Governments / UTs.  As such, the data regarding the number of 
awareness campaigns undertaken under the PCMA Act are maintained by the 
respective State Governments/ UT Administrations. 
     
In addition, the Central Government also undertakes awareness drives, media 
campaigns and outreach programmes and issues advisories to the States/ UTs from 
time to time to highlight the various issues about this evil practice. Further, the Ministry 
of Women and Child Developmen t implements the ‘Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP)’ 
scheme, wherein women and society at large are made aware about gender equality 
and ill effects of child marriages.  
     
Further, Government of India has introduced CHILDLINE with short code 1098, a 
24X7 telephone emergency outreach service for children in crisis, which responds with 
suitable interventions to calls for any form of assistance which a child requires, 
including for prevention of child marriages in coordination with police, CMPOs, District 
Child Protection Units etc.  
449

(c):   The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) undertakes 
various activities and programmes from time to time with concerned stakeholders/ 
organizations such as representatives of Child Welfare Committees (CW C), Police, 
Women and Child Development Department and Civil Society organizations on the 
issue of child marriages and related matters. Further, NCPCR requested all States/ UTs 
to issue directions to all stakeholders, including   Sarpanches and Civil Society 
Organizations to take proactive steps and preventive measures to stop child marriages 
on the occasion of Akshay Tritiya.  
     
In addition, the Commission organised 55 Benches / Camps in aspirational 
districts of various State/ UTs during 2019-20. With this proactive effort of taking all the 
stakeholders on board at district level, the Commission pointed out a number of issues 
related to child rights including child marriage before the district authorities, concerned 
officials and the respective State Commissions for Protection of Child Rights 
(SCPCRs). The Commission also heard a number of grievances during its camps in the 
districts. Visits, Inspections and interactions with children as well as community were 
also undertaken to understand the concerns of children. Further, the Commission took 
35 online Inter-Departmental Review Meetings with all State/ UTs during October –
November 2020. The Commission also carried out a detailed exercise to identify 
indicators based on various child-related legislations. The indicators were on 
programmes and provisions provided under the various Child related legislations 
including the issue of child marriages.

SHRI K.J. ALPHONS INDICATING STEPS TAKEN BY NCPCR REGARDING CHILD 
TRAFFICKING DURING THE LAST FIVE YEARS. 
 
1. NCPCR organized series of one day district level workshops on Combating 
Child Trafficking at various potential Source and Destination Hotspot districts 
of Assam, Manipur, Nagaland and West Tripura, NER.  
2. Virtual meetings to discuss the issue of Child Trafficking with SCPCRs of 
Source Hotspot States with State CPCRs of trafficking prone Hotspots States 
with focus on Eastern and North Eastern States of our country.  
 
3. National Level Multi- stakeholders E- Consultation meeting to Combat Child 
Trafficking Post Lockdown Situation due to COVID-19   
 
4. NCPCRs Document containing Recommendations on “Preventing Child 
Trafficking Post Lock Down “Due to COVID 19 Pandemic  based on the inputs 
received and observations made by the Commission through various meetings 
conducted virtually with SCPCRs, other stakeholders, various rescue 
operations conducted during lockdown period and inquiries taken up by the 
Commission. 
5. The Commission held three (3) One Day State Level Workshop on Preventing 
Child Trafficking during Extra Ordinary Situation of COVID 19 in the State of 
Manipur, Meghalaya and Tripura in September 2021.  
 
6. State level Orientation on the problems of Trafficking of Children and POCSO 
Act, 2012 in West Bengal to combat Child Trafficking and Protection of Children 
from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 in Kolkata on 19th December 2017 
 
7. Advisory to States to regulate placement agencies for prevention of trafficking 
and exploitation of children to Chief Secretaries of all States/UTs on 31 st 
January 2018 to take initiative to bring law to regulate placement agencies to 
prevent trafficking and exploitation of children. 
 
8. Quick Response Cell (QRC):NCPCR has constituted a Quick Response Cell 
(QRC) to address various issues requiring immediate redressal including 
instance of child trafficking. 
 
9. District-level Workshops on Combating Child Trafficking in Assam, Manipur, 
Tripura and Nagaland  with an objective to  (i) assess the current situation of 
child rights with focus on child trafficking effectiveness of the provisions of the 
Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, J. J. Act, IPC and other laws for the rescue 
and post-rescue work; (ii) sharing of experience amongst the concerned 
agencies with regard to rescue and post-rescue work; (iii) the involvement of 
NGOs; (iv) roles, responsibilities and functions of the various stakeholders; 
and(v) assess programmes, legislations and judicial interventions at the state 
level.

NATIONAL CRECHE SCHEMES 
  
  
948:   DR. AMAR PATNAIK: 
  
Will the Minister of Women & Child Development be pleased to state: 
  
(a) 
 number of creches set up in compliance with the National Creche Schemes 
and Maternity Benefit Act in organisations in the last three years; 
  
(b) 
 details of the measures undertaken to create awareness and removing other 
obstacles as Rajagopalan and Tabarrok (2019) estimate that less than 1 per 
cent of all women in the labour force benefit from the law; 
  
(c)  whether the non-functional and non-performing crèches out of the 23,293 
crèches in the country have been weeded out through intensive inspections 
by agencies according to the revised scheme; and 
  
(d) 
 if so, details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor? 
  
  
  
                                                        ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRIMATI SMRITI ZUBIN IRANI) 
 
(a) & (b)  The number of functional crèches under the ‘National Creche Scheme for 
the Children of Working Mothers’ in the country during the last three years is as 
under:  
  
During the Year Number of Creches 
2017-18 18040 
2018-19 8018 
2019-20 6458 
         
    The Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017 requires every establishment 
having fifty or more employees to have the facility of crèche within a prescribed 
distance. The State Governments, who are the appropriate Government under the 
Maternity Benefit Act for establishments other than mines and circus, are required to 
frame rules for the purposes of the Act, including inter alia for prescribing amenities 
and facilities required to be provided in such crèches, in light of which the Ministry of 
454

Labour and Employment has already requested all the State Governments on 
17.11.2017. In addition, Ministry of Women and Child Development has also issued 
directions/guidelines, from time to time, to the States and Union Territories on 
various aspects including inter alia for creating awareness  among the communities 
about the prescribed amenities and facilities to be provided in Creches.  
 
In this regard, a communication dated 02.11.2018 enclosing the National 
Minimum Guidelines for setting up and running crèches under  Maternity Benefit 
(Amendment) Act, 2017 was issued to the Ministries/Departments, States & UTs, 
advising the requisite know how to  set up model crèches facilities with adequate 
provisions, measures to be taken to create awareness about the Creche facilities 
among the communities and to promote willingness among working mothers to avail 
such facilities. Further, a letter dated 04.05.2021  was issued to States/UTs to 
ensure availability of crèche facilities, and to allow concerned women four visits a 
day to crèche and interval for rest in accordance with the legal provisions of the 
Maternity Benefit Act. No data in respect of firms employing more than fifty 
employees and where crèche is established is maintained centrally.  
    
(c ) & (d)   Decision for  running and continuation of operations of crèches is taken by 
State Governments and UT Administrations on the basis of verification and 
inspections got done by them. The Ministry of Women and Child Development, 
Government of India releases fund to States and UTs on receipt of proposals 
supported with necessary documentation and information from them. 
  
            The steps taken by Government for proper implementation of the ‘National 
Creche Scheme for the Children of Working Mothers’ include monit oring through 
inspections of crèches, verification of their operations, and follow ups through 
meetings, video conferences and discussions with the concerned officials of States 
and UTs.
